set_aside.subject: A16 refused confirmation state
set_aside.text: A refused confirmation keeps it, and the step may be shown again; a refused upload — too large or unreadable — replaces nothing. A refused import may be retried with a corrected file; nothing of a refused attempt remains.
set_aside.question: After confirmation is refused, does the session keep the uploaded file and confirmation step, or does nothing from the refused attempt remain?
options: Keep the uploaded file and permit the confirmation step to be shown again.
Drop the uploaded file and require another upload.
Keep only the uploaded file while clearing the pending confirmation step.
set_aside.default_guess: Follow the more specific rule 2: keep the uploaded file and allow the step to be shown again, interpreting rule 9 as saying only that no durable import result remains.

witness.initial: An owner session holds a mapped upload; before confirmation, production acquires an id that conflicts with a picked record.
events: Registry detects the conflict and refuses confirmation.
The owner asks to see the confirmation step again.
outcomes: Rule 2 keeps the upload and allows the step to be shown again.
Rule 9 leaves nothing of the refused attempt, so the owner must upload again.
witness.observer: The owner sees either the confirmation step again or a demand to re-upload the file.

set_aside.subject: A16 import timestamps
set_aside.text: An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers, the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry in one transaction.
set_aside.question: What authority supplies the import's fresh instant, and is it read once and shared by every new Customer, the migration closure and the audit entry, or read separately for those records?
options: Read one UTC-aware clock instant once and use it for every fresh timestamp written by the import.
Read the same clock separately for each created Customer, the closure and the audit entry.
Receive one authoritative import instant from the caller and use it for every fresh timestamp.
set_aside.default_guess: Read one UTC-aware system-clock instant once after validation and use it for all fresh timestamps in the transaction.

witness.initial: A valid confirmed import will create two Customers, one migration closure and one audit entry.
events: The owner reads the Customers and audit log.
outcomes: All four records carry one identical import instant.
The records carry slightly different instants because the clock was read for each write.
witness.observer: The owner sees equal or unequal timestamps in the stored records and audit view.

set_aside.subject: A16 file digest semantics
set_aside.text: The mapping names the file by its digest.
set_aside.question: Which digest algorithm defines the file identity, what exact bytes are covered, and what collision-resistance guarantee is required?
options: SHA-256 over exactly the received file-part bytes.
SHA-512 over exactly the received file-part bytes.
A different deterministic digest, with its algorithm and covered bytes declared.
set_aside.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over exactly the received file-part bytes and require collision-resistant binding of the mapping, closure and audit entry to those bytes.

witness.initial: The owner uploads one valid export file.
events: Registry computes its digest and shows the mapping.
Registry stores the digest in the closure and audit entry.
outcomes: One implementation records the SHA-256 digest of the file bytes.
Another records a different algorithm's digest or includes multipart framing in the covered bytes.
witness.observer: The owner and any reader of the migration closure or audit entry see different file identities.

set_aside.subject: A16 digest representation in contracts
set_aside.text: The mapping names the file by its digest.
set_aside.question: How is the decided digest represented in mapping, closure and audit contract values?
options: A structured value carrying an algorithm name and encoded digest.
consequences: A bare encoding is compact but requires the algorithm to be fixed elsewhere.
A structured value permits algorithm evolution but changes result and persistence contract shapes.
Different encodings produce incompatible visible and serialized values even when they cover identical bytes.
set_aside.requirement: The mapping names the file by its digest.

set_aside.subject: A16 conflict atomicity invariant test
set_aside.text: A file whose one pointer id production holds refuses the whole import.
set_aside.question: Which Required tests item must explicitly show the formal invariant `conflict at confirmation => store unchanged`, including that no project, room, pointer, Customer, closure or audit entry is written?
options: Extend this test to read the store after the conflict and assert that every affected record kind is unchanged.
Add a separate confirmation-conflict atomicity test that asserts the complete unchanged-store result.
set_aside.default_guess: Extend this test with explicit assertions that the store and audit log are unchanged after the confirmation conflict.

set_aside.subject: A02 blank-value classification
set_aside.text: A required value given as an empty string or as white space only is missing, and the action is refused as for a missing value
set_aside.question: Which exact set of characters counts as white space for deciding whether a supplied value is missing?
options: The runtime language's `strip` semantics, fixed to a named runtime version.
set_aside.default_guess: Use the Unicode White_Space property and state the normalization/version rule explicitly.

witness.initial: No project with the proposed id exists.
events: The owner creates a project whose display name consists only of U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE.
outcomes: Unicode whitespace handling treats the name as missing and refuses creation.
ASCII-only handling treats the name as present and creates the project.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a missing-value refusal or a newly created project.
